rationale:
The supplied proof contains three separable mathematical obligations and a combinatorial assembly.

The three children:
1. subspace_eq_of_inter_ball is step 1: a linear subspace is determined by its trace on a ball about one of its points. This is reusable linear algebra and metric reasoning.
2. great_circle_local_plane is steps 2–3, the continuation argument along a great circle. It uses openness of the agreement set, closedness of S, local planarity together with child 1, and connectedness of Q ∩ 𝕊 via isConnected_sphere. This is the only topological core. It is also the only part that needs the extra pinned import Mathlib.Analysis.Normed.Module.Connected; accepted commit bff81d31e is a precedent for adding pinned Mathlib imports.
3. planes_eq_or_inf_bot is steps 4–5 plus the core of step 8: two seeded 2-planes are equal or meet only at 0. This is Simon's printed claim P_i ∩ P_j = {0} (chapter-07.txt lines 502–504).

The parent keeps steps 0, 6, 7, 9 and the assembly part of step 8:
- choose δ_p and Q_p, and note p ∈ Q_p;
- S ∩ sphere 0 1 is compact (isCompact_sphere, IsCompact.inter_left), and IsCompact.elim_nhds_subcover gives a Finset t;
- the planes are t.image Q, enumerated by Finset.equivFin;
- finrank 2 comes from the hypothesis;
- for i ≠ j, Ps i ⊓ Ps j = ⊥ follows from child 3 seeded at the chosen p, p' ∈ t;
- the covering of S ∖ {0} follows from dilation.
Every child conclusion is used, and dependencies are acyclic: 1 → 2, then {1, 2} → 3, and the parent uses 3.

subproblems.title: Two linear subspaces that agree on a ball about a common point are equal
subproblems.statement: Let P ∈ ℕ, let Q₁ and Q₂ be linear subspaces of ℝ^P, let x ∈ Q₁ and t > 0. If Q₁ ∩ B_t(x) = Q₂ ∩ B_t(x), where B_t(x) is the open ball of radius t about x, then Q₁ = Q₂.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P : ℕ) (Q₁ Q₂ : Submodule ℝ (Euclid P)) (x : Euclid P) (t : ℝ), x ∈ Q₁ → 0 < t → (Q₁ : Set (Euclid P)) ∩ ball x t = (Q₂ : Set (Euclid P)) ∩ ball x t → Q₁ = Q₂
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 1 (uniqueness of planes) of the supplied proof of idtp_tdc_cone_set_finite_planes, which details Simon's claim in the proof of 7.3.3(1) (chapter-07.txt lines 502-504) that spt S0 lies in finitely many 2-planes P_i with P_i ∩ P_j = {0}. Notation: B_t(x) = {y : |y − x| < t} (Mathlib `ball x t`); Q₁, Q₂ are also viewed as subsets of ℝ^P. No dimension hypothesis is needed.
1. (x ∈ Q₂.) Since |x − x| = 0 < t, x ∈ Q₁ ∩ B_t(x) = Q₂ ∩ B_t(x); hence x ∈ Q₂.
2. (One inclusion, in general form.) Let A, B be linear subspaces of ℝ^P with x ∈ A, x ∈ B and A ∩ B_t(x) = B ∩ B_t(x). We show A ⊆ B. Let v ∈ A and put s := t/(2(|v| + 1)). Then s > 0 and s|v| ≤ s(|v| + 1) = t/2 < t. The point y := x + s·v lies in A (A contains x and s·v and is closed under addition), and |y − x| = |s·v| = s|v| < t, so y ∈ A ∩ B_t(x) = B ∩ B_t(x), i.e. y ∈ B. As x ∈ B, s·v = y − x ∈ B, and therefore v = s⁻¹·(s·v) ∈ B.
3. (Conclusion.) Step 2 with (A, B) := (Q₁, Q₂), using x ∈ Q₁, x ∈ Q₂ (step 1) and the hypothesis Q₁ ∩ B_t(x) = Q₂ ∩ B_t(x), gives Q₁ ≤ Q₂. Step 2 with (A, B) := (Q₂, Q₁), using the reversed equality Q₂ ∩ B_t(x) = Q₁ ∩ B_t(x), gives Q₂ ≤ Q₁. By antisymmetry of ≤ on submodules, Q₁ = Q₂. ∎
(Lean pointers: Metric.mem_ball_self, Submodule.add_mem / smul_mem / sub_mem, norm_smul, Real.norm_of_nonneg, smul_smul, inv_mul_cancel₀, le_antisymm.)
proof_key_steps: x lies in Q₁ ∩ B_t(x) = Q₂ ∩ B_t(x), so x ∈ Q₂.
For v ∈ Q₁ and s = t/(2(|v|+1)) > 0, the point x + s·v lies in Q₁ ∩ B_t(x) = Q₂ ∩ B_t(x), so s·v = (x + s·v) − x ∈ Q₂ and v = s⁻¹·(s·v) ∈ Q₂.
The same argument with Q₁ and Q₂ exchanged, and antisymmetry of ≤, give Q₁ = Q₂.

subproblems.title: Agreement of a closed locally planar set with a 2-plane near one unit point propagates along the whole great circle
subproblems.statement: Let P ∈ ℕ and let S ⊆ ℝ^P be a closed set such that every p ∈ S with p ≠ 0 has δ > 0 and a 2-dimensional linear subspace Q' of ℝ^P with S ∩ B_δ(p) = Q' ∩ B_δ(p). Let Q be a 2-dimensional linear subspace of ℝ^P, and suppose some x₀ ∈ Q with |x₀| = 1 and some ε₀ > 0 satisfy S ∩ B_ε₀(x₀) = Q ∩ B_ε₀(x₀). Then every x ∈ Q with |x| = 1 has some ε > 0 with S ∩ B_ε(x) = Q ∩ B_ε(x).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P : ℕ) (S : Set (Euclid P)) (Q : Submodule ℝ (Euclid P)) (x₀ : Euclid P) (ε₀ : ℝ), IsClosed S → (∀ p ∈ S, p ≠ 0 → ∃ (δ : ℝ) (Q' : Submodule ℝ (Euclid P)), 0 < δ ∧ Module.finrank ℝ Q' = 2 ∧ S ∩ ball p δ = (Q' : Set (Euclid P)) ∩ ball p δ) → Module.finrank ℝ Q = 2 → x₀ ∈ Q → ‖x₀‖ = 1 → 0 < ε₀ → S ∩ ball x₀ ε₀ = (Q : Set (Euclid P)) ∩ ball x₀ ε₀ → ∀ x : Euclid P, x ∈ Q → ‖x‖ = 1 → ∃ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε ∧ S ∩ ball x ε = (Q : Set (Euclid P)) ∩ ball x ε
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: steps 2-3 (points where S is locally a given plane; whole great circles) of the supplied proof of idtp_tdc_cone_set_finite_planes. Notation: B_r(y) = ball y r; 𝕊 := {y ∈ ℝ^P : |y| = 1} (Mathlib `sphere 0 1`); K := Q ∩ 𝕊; A := {y ∈ ℝ^P : there is ε > 0 with S ∩ B_ε(y) = Q ∩ B_ε(y)}. The claim to prove is K ⊆ A.
1. (K is connected.) As finrank Q = 2, Q is finite-dimensional (Module.finite_of_finrank_eq_succ) and Module.rank ℝ Q = 2 > 1 (Module.finrank_eq_rank). Q with the norm restricted from ℝ^P is a real normed space, so by Mathlib's isConnected_sphere (file Mathlib/Analysis/Normed/Module/Connected.lean; that module is not imported by the frozen header, so the implementation adds the pinned import `import Mathlib.Analysis.Normed.Module.Connected` to Submission.lean, exactly as accepted Ch07 commits such as bff81d31e added other pinned Mathlib imports) the unit sphere {z ∈ Q : |z| = 1} of Q is connected. Its image under the continuous inclusion Q → ℝ^P (Subtype.val, continuous_subtype_val) is exactly K: an element z of Q has the same norm in Q and in ℝ^P, and every y ∈ K is the image of ⟨y, y ∈ Q⟩. A continuous image of a connected set is connected (IsConnected.image), so K is connected, in particular preconnected.
2. (A is open.) Let y ∈ A, with ε > 0 and S ∩ B_ε(y) = Q ∩ B_ε(y), and let y' ∈ B_ε(y), d := |y' − y| < ε. Put ε' := ε − d > 0. Then B_ε'(y') ⊆ B_ε(y) because ε' + d ≤ ε (Metric.ball_subset_ball'), so S ∩ B_ε'(y') = (S ∩ B_ε(y)) ∩ B_ε'(y') = (Q ∩ B_ε(y)) ∩ B_ε'(y') = Q ∩ B_ε'(y'), i.e. y' ∈ A. Hence B_ε(y) ⊆ A, and A is open (Metric.isOpen_iff).
3. (A ∩ Q ⊆ S.) If y ∈ A ∩ Q, with ε as in the definition of A, then y ∈ Q ∩ B_ε(y) = S ∩ B_ε(y), so y ∈ S.
4. (Points of K outside A are not in the closure of A ∩ Q.) Let x ∈ K with x ∉ A. We find r > 0 such that no y ∈ A ∩ Q satisfies |x − y| < r; by Metric.mem_closure_iff this means x ∉ closure(A ∩ Q).
 (a) Case x ∉ S. S is closed, so its complement is open and some r > 0 has B_r(x) ∩ S = ∅. If some y ∈ A ∩ Q had |x − y| < r, then y ∈ S by step 3 and y ∈ B_r(x), a contradiction.
 (b) Case x ∈ S. Since |x| = 1, x ≠ 0, so the local-planarity hypothesis gives δ > 0 and a subspace Q' with S ∩ B_δ(x) = Q' ∩ B_δ(x) (the dimension of Q' is not used). Then Q' ≠ Q, since Q' = Q would put x in A (with ε := δ). Take r := δ/2 and suppose y ∈ A ∩ Q with |x − y| < δ/2, witnessed by ε_y > 0 with S ∩ B_ε_y(y) = Q ∩ B_ε_y(y). Let τ := min(ε_y, δ/2) > 0. Then B_τ(y) ⊆ B_ε_y(y), and B_τ(y) ⊆ B_δ(x) because τ + |y − x| < δ/2 + δ/2 = δ. Consequently
 Q ∩ B_τ(y) = (Q ∩ B_ε_y(y)) ∩ B_τ(y) = (S ∩ B_ε_y(y)) ∩ B_τ(y) = S ∩ B_τ(y) = (S ∩ B_δ(x)) ∩ B_τ(y) = (Q' ∩ B_δ(x)) ∩ B_τ(y) = Q' ∩ B_τ(y).
 Since y ∈ Q and τ > 0, the sibling theorem idtp_tdc_csfp_subspace_eq_of_inter_ball (applied to P, Q, Q', y, τ) gives Q = Q', contradicting Q' ≠ Q.
5. (Connectedness.) Let u := A and v := ℝ^P ∖ closure(A ∩ Q); both are open (step 2; complement of a closed set). Every point of K lies in u or, by step 4, in v; so K ⊆ u ∪ v. K ∩ u is nonempty: x₀ ∈ Q and |x₀| = 1 give x₀ ∈ K, and ε₀ > 0 with S ∩ B_ε₀(x₀) = Q ∩ B_ε₀(x₀) gives x₀ ∈ A. Suppose some x ∈ K is not in A. Then x ∈ v by step 4, so K ∩ v ≠ ∅, and preconnectedness of K (step 1; the definition of IsPreconnected applied to u, v) yields z ∈ K ∩ (u ∩ v). But z ∈ K ⊆ Q and z ∈ A, so z ∈ A ∩ Q ⊆ closure(A ∩ Q) (subset_closure), contradicting z ∈ v. Therefore K ⊆ A.
6. (Conclusion.) Let x ∈ Q with |x| = 1. Then x ∈ K ⊆ A, i.e. there is ε > 0 with S ∩ B_ε(x) = Q ∩ B_ε(x). ∎
proof_key_steps: The great circle K = Q ∩ 𝕊 is connected: it is the image under the inclusion Q → ℝ^P of the unit sphere of the 2-dimensional normed space Q (isConnected_sphere, IsConnected.image).
The set A of points near which S coincides with Q is open, and A ∩ Q ⊆ S.

A point of K outside A has a ball disjoint from A ∩ Q: by closedness of S if the point is not in S, and otherwise by local planarity at the point together with idtp_tdc_csfp_subspace_eq_of_inter_ball.
Preconnectedness of K applied to the open sets A and ℝ^P ∖ closure(A ∩ Q), with the seed x₀ ∈ K ∩ A, gives K ⊆ A.

subproblems.title: Two seeded 2-planes of a closed locally planar set are equal or meet only at 0
subproblems.statement: Let P ∈ ℕ and let S ⊆ ℝ^P be a closed set such that every p ∈ S with p ≠ 0 has δ > 0 and a 2-dimensional linear subspace Q of ℝ^P with S ∩ B_δ(p) = Q ∩ B_δ(p). Let Q₁, Q₂ be 2-dimensional linear subspaces of ℝ^P, let p₁ ∈ Q₁ and p₂ ∈ Q₂ with |p₁| = |p₂| = 1, and let δ₁, δ₂ > 0 with S ∩ B_δ₁(p₁) = Q₁ ∩ B_δ₁(p₁) and S ∩ B_δ₂(p₂) = Q₂ ∩ B_δ₂(p₂). Then Q₁ = Q₂ or Q₁ ∩ Q₂ = {0} (Q₁ ⊓ Q₂ = ⊥).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P : ℕ) (S : Set (Euclid P)) (Q₁ Q₂ : Submodule ℝ (Euclid P)) (p₁ p₂ : Euclid P) (δ₁ δ₂ : ℝ), IsClosed S → (∀ p ∈ S, p ≠ 0 → ∃ (δ : ℝ) (Q : Submodule ℝ (Euclid P)), 0 < δ ∧ Module.finrank ℝ Q = 2 ∧ S ∩ ball p δ = (Q : Set (Euclid P)) ∩ ball p δ) → Module.finrank ℝ Q₁ = 2 → Module.finrank ℝ Q₂ = 2 → p₁ ∈ Q₁ → ‖p₁‖ = 1 → 0 < δ₁ → S ∩ ball p₁ δ₁ = (Q₁ : Set (Euclid P)) ∩ ball p₁ δ₁ → p₂ ∈ Q₂ → ‖p₂‖ = 1 → 0 < δ₂ → S ∩ ball p₂ δ₂ = (Q₂ : Set (Euclid P)) ∩ ball p₂ δ₂ → Q₁ = Q₂ ∨ Q₁ ⊓ Q₂ = ⊥
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: steps 4, 5 and the core of step 8 of the supplied proof of idtp_tdc_cone_set_finite_planes (the great circles through two seeds are equal or disjoint, so distinct planes meet only in 0). Notation: B_r(y) = ball y r.
1. (Reduction.) If Q₁ ⊓ Q₂ = ⊥, the right disjunct holds. Otherwise, by Submodule.ne_bot_iff there is v ∈ Q₁ ⊓ Q₂ with v ≠ 0, and by Submodule.mem_inf, v ∈ Q₁ and v ∈ Q₂. We prove the left disjunct Q₁ = Q₂.
2. (A common unit vector.) Since v ≠ 0, |v| > 0. Put u := |v|⁻¹·v. Then |u| = |v|⁻¹·|v| = 1, and u ∈ Q₁, u ∈ Q₂ because subspaces are closed under scalar multiplication.
3. (S is locally Q₁ and locally Q₂ at u.) The sibling theorem idtp_tdc_csfp_great_circle_local_plane applied to (P, S, Q₁, x₀ := p₁, ε₀ := δ₁) has hypotheses IsClosed S, the local-planarity hypothesis (verbatim the one assumed here), finrank Q₁ = 2, p₁ ∈ Q₁, |p₁| = 1, 0 < δ₁ and S ∩ B_δ₁(p₁) = Q₁ ∩ B_δ₁(p₁), all given; evaluated at x := u (u ∈ Q₁, |u| = 1) it yields ε₁ > 0 with S ∩ B_ε₁(u) = Q₁ ∩ B_ε₁(u). In the same way, applied to (P, S, Q₂, p₂, δ₂) and evaluated at u (u ∈ Q₂, |u| = 1), it yields ε₂ > 0 with S ∩ B_ε₂(u) = Q₂ ∩ B_ε₂(u).
4. (Q₁ and Q₂ agree near u.) Let t := min(ε₁, ε₂) > 0. Then B_t(u) ⊆ B_ε₁(u) and B_t(u) ⊆ B_ε₂(u) (Metric.ball_subset_ball), so
 Q₁ ∩ B_t(u) = (Q₁ ∩ B_ε₁(u)) ∩ B_t(u) = (S ∩ B_ε₁(u)) ∩ B_t(u) = S ∩ B_t(u) = (S ∩ B_ε₂(u)) ∩ B_t(u) = (Q₂ ∩ B_ε₂(u)) ∩ B_t(u) = Q₂ ∩ B_t(u).
5. (Conclusion.) Since u ∈ Q₁ and t > 0, the sibling theorem idtp_tdc_csfp_subspace_eq_of_inter_ball applied to (P, Q₁, Q₂, u, t) gives Q₁ = Q₂. ∎
proof_key_steps: If Q₁ ⊓ Q₂ ≠ ⊥, normalise a nonzero common vector to a unit vector u ∈ Q₁ ∩ Q₂.
idtp_tdc_csfp_great_circle_local_plane, seeded at (p₁, δ₁) resp. (p₂, δ₂), gives balls about u on which S equals Q₁ resp. Q₂.
On the smaller of the two balls Q₁ and Q₂ agree, so idtp_tdc_csfp_subspace_eq_of_inter_ball gives Q₁ = Q₂.
